pageShell.text: MF Matthew Fogarty Contact Home About Systems Featured Gallery Contact PLAYER DEVELOPMENT CASE STUDY Anaya Beard Anaya Beard's development shows what structured individualized development can build. Film feedback, skill tracking and early-morning work rebuilt key pieces of her game. A detailed progression plan helped her become one of the state's top players. Built to show how Coach Fogarty teaches, develops, tracks and raises the standard. PORTFOLIO HIGHLIGHT Start | Process | Lead | Stats | Awards | Next 350+ Hours Early Morning Work Athlete of Year Major Recognition OEC OPOY Conference Award 2x First Team All-Conference DI/DII Offers Full-Ride Opportunities 2x Captain Leadership Standard 01 / FOUNDATION Building From The Starting Point The work began with Anaya's raw tools, athletic upside and the habits that needed to be rebuilt before her game could fully translate. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. She had the motor, athleticism and versatility to become an impact player, but the early stage was about establishing a player-development baseline. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. San Antonio - State Playoffs Rd 2 32 points 10 rebounds vs. #19 Santa Barbara 29 points 19 rebounds vs. #23 LA Trade-Tech 28 points 9 rebounds, 2 steals vs. #10 Saddleback 23 points 20 rebounds vs. #2 Orange Coast, 2024 state champion Mid-range jumper Contact finish Catch-and-shoot three Drive right High post jab Fast-break floating finish View More 05 / ACCOLADES RECOGNITION The Recognition Came From The Work The awards tell the outcome, but the case study is about the process that made those outcomes possible. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. The next-level interest is the result of the process: habits rebuilt, role expanded, leadership proven and production sustained. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. pageShell.text: MF Matthew Fogarty Contact Home About Systems Featured Gallery Contact PLAYER DEVELOPMENT CASE STUDY Anaya Beard Anaya Beard's development shows what structured individualized development can build. Film feedback, skill tracking and early-morning work rebuilt key pieces of her game. A detailed progression plan helped her become one of the state's top players. Built to show how Coach Fogarty teaches, develops, tracks and raises the standard. PORTFOLIO HIGHLIGHT Start | Process | Lead | Stats | Awards | Next 350+ Hours Early Morning Work Athlete of Year Major Recognition OEC OPOY Conference Award 2x First Team All-Conference DI/DII Offers Full-Ride Opportunities 2x Captain Leadership Standard 01 / FOUNDATION Building From The Starting Point The work began with Anaya's raw tools, athletic upside and the habits that needed to be rebuilt before her game could fully translate. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. She had the motor, athleticism and versatility to become an impact player, but the early stage was about establishing a player-development baseline. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. San Antonio - State Playoffs Rd 2 32 points 10 rebounds vs. #19 Santa Barbara 29 points 19 rebounds vs. #23 LA Trade-Tech 28 points 9 rebounds, 2 steals vs. #10 Saddleback 23 points 20 rebounds vs. #2 Orange Coast, 2024 state champion Mid-range jumper Contact finish Catch-and-shoot three Drive right High post jab Fast-break floating finish View More 05 / ACCOLADES RECOGNITION The Recognition Came From The Work The awards tell the outcome, but the case study is about the process that made those outcomes possible. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. The next-level interest is the result of the process: habits rebuilt, role expanded, leadership proven and production sustained. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. Film feedback, skill tracking and early-morning work rebuilt key pieces of her game. A detailed progression plan helped her become one of the state's top players. Built to show how Coach Fogarty teaches, develops, tracks and raises the standard. PORTFOLIO HIGHLIGHT Start | Process | Lead | Stats | Awards | Next 350+ Hours Early Morning Work Athlete of Year Major Recognition OEC OPOY Conference Award 2x First Team All-Conference DI/DII Offers Full-Ride Opportunities 2x Captain Leadership Standard 01 / FOUNDATION Building From The Starting Point The work began with Anaya's raw tools, athletic upside and the habits that needed to be rebuilt before her game could fully translate. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. She had the motor, athleticism and versatility to become an impact player, but the early stage was about establishing a player-development baseline. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. San Antonio - State Playoffs Rd 2 32 points 10 rebounds vs. #19 Santa Barbara 29 points 19 rebounds vs. #23 LA Trade-Tech 28 points 9 rebounds, 2 steals vs. #10 Saddleback 23 points 20 rebounds vs. #2 Orange Coast, 2024 state champion Mid-range jumper Contact finish Catch-and-shoot three Drive right High post jab Fast-break floating finish View More 05 / ACCOLADES RECOGNITION The Recognition Came From The Work The awards tell the outcome, but the case study is about the process that made those outcomes possible. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. Film feedback, skill tracking and early-morning work rebuilt key pieces of her game. A detailed progression plan helped her become one of the state's top players. Built to show how Coach Fogarty teaches, develops, tracks and raises the standard. PORTFOLIO HIGHLIGHT Start | Process | Lead | Stats | Awards | Next 350+ Hours Early Morning Work Athlete of Year Major Recognition OEC OPOY Conference Award 2x First Team All-Conference DI/DII Offers Full-Ride Opportunities 2x Captain Leadership Standard 01 / FOUNDATION Building From The Starting Point The work began with Anaya's raw tools, athletic upside and the habits that needed to be rebuilt before her game could fully translate. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. She had the motor, athleticism and versatility to become an impact player, but the early stage was about establishing a player-development baseline. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. San Antonio - State Playoffs Rd 2 32 points 10 rebounds vs. #19 Santa Barbara 29 points 19 rebounds vs. #23 LA Trade-Tech 28 points 9 rebounds, 2 steals vs. #10 Saddleback 23 points 20 rebounds vs. #2 Orange Coast, 2024 state champion Mid-range jumper Contact finish Catch-and-shoot three Drive right High post jab Fast-break floating finish View More 05 / ACCOLADES RECOGNITION The Recognition Came From The Work The awards tell the outcome, but the case study is about the process that made those outcomes possible. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first. Anaya entered the process as a 6'0 forward with a 3.4 GPA and a Nursing / Public Health / Biology pathway. Starting point and skill foundation Raw tools shaped into repeatable habits Learning expectations, standards and daily detail Foundation for efficient three-level scoring, rebounding and defensive versatility Development Lens The foundation stage shows where Coach Fogarty first started working with Anaya and why the development process needed to be structured, patient and detailed. First workout ever First workout photo montage Baseline shooting form Baseline jump shot Baseline left-hand finish Baseline fadeaway View More 02 / DEVELOPMENT PROCESS The Early Mornings, Repetition And Grind Behind The Growth The breakthrough was built through a structured player-development system, film-based feedback, skill tracking and consistent work outside team practice. Anaya completed 350+ voluntary early morning development hours outside team practice. The process used offseason structure, repeated correction, film-based feedback and progressions designed to rebuild her game from the ground up. 350+ voluntary early morning development hours Skill tracking and film-based feedback Offseason structure through summers, weekends and holidays Rebuilt habits connected directly to game transfer Coach-Led Structure This stage is the clearest example of the development system: identify the gap, teach the detail, repeat the correction, measure the progress and connect the skill to live basketball. Early morning development work Shot release repetition video Footwork repetition video Shooting form training Catch-and-shoot training Archer shooting development View More 03 / LEADERSHIP IMPACT The Turning Point Became A Program Standard As the work started to click, Anaya's growth carried into leadership, culture and the daily standard of the program. Anaya became a two-time team captain and helped transform Santa Ana College into a back-to-back state playoff program. Her consistency influenced teammates because the standard was visible: early work, weekends, holidays and a willingness to be coached. 2x team captain Program standard setter Helped Santa Ana College reach back-to-back state playoff appearances Work ethic raised the level around her Program Impact The case study is not only about individual skill. It also shows how player development can change the way a player leads, competes and affects a team environment. Bench celebration Helping teammate up Sideline energy Teammate high-five Court leadership Team celebration View More 04 / BREAKTHROUGH PRODUCTION Growth That Transferred Against High-Level Competition The development process showed up in production against top-ranked opponents, playoff pressure and elite frontcourt matchups. 38 points 15/20 FG, 7 rebounds vs. #1 Mt. Anaya became Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year, a two-time First Team All-Conference selection, a two-time team captain and a two-time Most Inspirational Award recipient. Orange Empire Conference Offensive Player of the Year 2x First Team All-Conference 2x Team Captain 2x Most Inspirational Award Academic credibility through a 3.4 GPA and health-science pathway Earned Outcomes The recognition matters because it came after the daily development habits, leadership growth and production against real competition. Scholar Athlete of the Year 500 Point Club First Team All-Conference and OPOY Back-to-back First Team All-Conference Athlete of the Week Awards ceremony recognition View More 06 / NEXT-LEVEL OPPORTUNITIES A Forward/Wing Projection Backed By Growth, Production And Toughness The final stage of the journey connects the development process to recruiting outcomes and a clear college projection. Anaya's growth produced multiple Division I and Division II full-ride scholarship opportunities. Her college projection is built on leadership, production, toughness, defensive versatility and measurable player-development growth. Full game film, stat sheets, academic information and Synergy access are available. View Player Portfolio Contact Coach Fogarty Recruiting Lens This is still a development case study first.
